title: SKP Business / Pipeline
description: Business / pipeline counters across the three services that emit domain meters (orchestrator / keeper / processor), plus the WebApi represented by ASP.NET Core request metrics only (it registers no domain meter - BPD-03). The two template variables are populated from the process_runtime_dotnet_* family emitted by OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Runtime 1.15.0 on net8.0 (research F-1) - the one instrumentation every service class shares. A future net9.0 upgrade would rename that family to dotnet_* and blank both dropdowns; scripts/phase-87-dashboard-lint.ps1 rule S8 hard-fails on any dotnet_* reference so that regression surfaces hermetically in ~5s instead of as a silently empty dashboard.

panels.title: Orchestrator consumed vs sent (conservation)
panels.description: Overlaying consumed and sent on one axis is what makes the conservation relationship readable at a glance (BPD-02). Both targets are Class A (VER-01): they have live series on a healthy stack and must never carry an or vector(0) guard - lint rule C7 enforces that, because a guarded Class A signal renders 0 and lets a fully stalled pipeline pass the live proof.

panels.title: Keeper consumed vs sent (conservation)
panels.description: GUARDED ON PURPOSE - both targets carry 'or vector(0)', and that is not decoration. keeper_messages_consumed / keeper_messages_sent increment ONLY inside RecoveryConsumerBase.Consume / CountSent, so they fire only during a recovery event: research F-4 measured zero live series and Pitfall 6 records that both names are absent from the entire 15-day Prometheus __name__ index. That places them in REQUIREMENTS.md VER-01 Class B ('any counter with no live series on a healthy stack'), so this is a properly guarded Class-B panel, not a Class-A panel with a hole in it. Lint rule C3 requires the guard on EVERY expression referencing these two counters anywhere in this file, and plan 87-05 STEP F classifies an expression Class A or Class B purely by the presence of this substring - its traffic drive (STEP E) is a happy-path FanOutSeeder run with no fault scenario, so an unguarded target here would be asserted as Class A and would fail the live proof. HOW TO READ A FLAT 0: 'no recovery traffic in this window'. It does NOT mean 'keeper down' - the keeper liveness signal is the Class-A 'Keeper L2 probe heartbeat' panel.

panels.title: Processor consumed vs sent by image (conservation)
panels.description: The VAR-04 correction in force (research F-6). Every source="processor" series carries the unresolved_0.0.0 MLBL-03 sentinel on service_name, so service_name CANNOT discriminate processor images; identityName (carrying {db.Name}_{db.Version}) is the discriminator, and it exists only on these two business counters. No processor panel on this dashboard groups by service_name - lint rule C5 enforces the identityName grouping. Both targets are Class A (VER-01): they have live series on a healthy stack and must never carry an 'or vector(0)' guard, which lint rule C7 enforces.

panels.title: Cross-tier conservation gap (orchestrator sent - processor consumed)
panels.description: This is the axis the 7-scenario resilience sweep scores on (MG-1 conservation), evaluated over the dashboard window rather than over a sweep run. A sustained positive value means the orchestrator dispatched work the processors never consumed. Class A (VER-01): both counters have live series on a healthy stack, so this expression carries NO 'or vector(0)' guard - lint rule C7 enforces that, because a guarded Class-A expression renders 0 and would let a fully stalled pipeline pass the live proof. Threshold: green base, red at 1 - the operand is an integer message count, so 'red above 0' is 'red at 1'.

panels.title: Per-processor dispatch gap
panels.description: The analyzer's historical bottleneck view expressed in the current counter names: dispatched-minus-consumed per processor identity. processorId is the DB identity GUID carried on both business counters - note it is a LABEL, not a metric, and it does not match the lint's processor_\w+ family regex because that regex requires the underscore (pinned by the lint's -SelfTest fixture (e)). Class A (VER-01): unguarded by design, enforced by lint rule C7.

panels.title: Orchestrator unresolved steps in range
panels.description: DEDICATED fault panel (BPD-02, lint rule C2): its targets reference orchestrator_step_unresolved_total and nothing else, so the indicator is never buried as one series inside a combined graph. GUARDED (VER-01 Class B, lint rule C3): an OTel counter is not exported to Prometheus until its first increment, and a healthy stack should have zero unresolved steps - research F-4 measured 0 live series. Without 'or vector(0)' this panel renders 'No data', which a reviewer reads as 'no faults' when it actually means 'the panel is broken' (threat T-87-16). With the guard it renders an honest 0. Threshold: green base, red at 1 - the value is an integer step count, so 'red above 0' is 'red at 1'.

panels.title: Processor dropped spawns in range
panels.description: DEDICATED fault panel (BPD-02, lint rule C2): a single metric only. GUARDED (VER-01 Class B, lint rule C3): processor_spawn_dropped_total has 0 live series on a healthy stack (research F-4) - it IS present in the 15-day __name__ index, so it has fired historically, but a green stack should drop zero spawns. Without the guard the panel renders 'No data' and is misread as 'no drops' (threat T-87-16). Threshold: green base, red at 1 - the value is an integer drop count, so 'red above 0' is 'red at 1'.

panels.title: Keeper consumed - sent gap in range
panels.description: DEDICATED keeper fault panel (BPD-02 as amended, lint rule C2 matches this stat - not the timeseries conservation overlay - because its targets reference exactly the two keeper message counters). WHAT IT IS NOT: this is deliberately titled for the gap it computes, not for a reinject / drop-outcome breakdown, because NO SUCH COUNTER EXISTS. Phase 74 removed the legacy label-less reinject-drop counter in favour of the uniform consumed/sent pair, leaving keeper_messages_consumed, keeper_messages_sent and keeper_l2_probe as the keeper's only three instruments (KeeperMetrics.cs:50-52, research F-5). Reinject outcome now lives solely in Elasticsearch as attributes.ReinjectOutcome, and ES panels are out of scope for this milestone. GUARDED (VER-01 Class B, lint rule C3): both counters increment only during a recovery event and are absent from the entire 15-day __name__ index (Pitfall 6), so the guard is what makes a healthy stack render 0 instead of 'No data'. Threshold: green base, red at 1 - the value is an integer message count.

panels.title: Keeper L2 probe heartbeat
panels.description: The 'keeper is alive and probing' heartbeat that accompanies the gap panel above; a healthy keeper holds this above zero. UNGUARDED ON PURPOSE - this is a VER-01 Class A signal. Unlike the three guarded fault stats and unlike the guarded keeper conservation overlay (panel 2), keeper_l2_probe_total HAS live series on a healthy stack (research: 2 series live), which is exactly why it is the panel that distinguishes 'keeper idle' from 'keeper dead'. Adding 'or vector(0)' here would demote it to Class B in plan 87-05's mechanical classifier and let a DEAD keeper render 0 and pass the live proof (threat T-87-20), so lint rule C7 forbids the guard on this expression.

panels.title: WebApi request rate by route
panels.description: BPD-03: the WebApi is represented on this dashboard by ASP.NET Core request metrics ONLY. It registers neither a domain meter nor the MassTransit meter, so adding domain counters here is explicitly out of scope - no panel in this row references any *_messages_*, *_step_unresolved_*, *_spawn_dropped_* or *_l2_probe_* counter. CAVEAT (BPD-03, research 'WebApi row'): the OTel collector DROPS every http.server.request.duration datapoint whose http.route starts with /health/ (k8s/02-configmaps.yaml:64-69), so on an idle stack only the orchestration endpoints appear and this row stays near-empty (2 series, _count = 2) until traffic is driven. Driving that traffic before asserting VER-01 is exactly what plan 87-05 does. NOTE ON THE LINT: http_route here is a LABEL name, not a metric name; the lint's Get-MetricTokens treats a family-prefixed token as a metric only when the next non-space character is '{', so it lands in the Bare set and is accepted by rule S15 as a KNOWN_LABEL. If rule S9 ever rejects it, the position scoping has regressed - re-run the lint with -SelfTest (fixtures (a)-(d) pin exactly these four expression shapes) and fix the script, never these panels.

panels.title: WebApi p95 request duration by route
panels.description: p95 over the ASP.NET Core request-duration histogram, per route. The ASP.NET Core histogram is in SECONDS (unlike the MassTransit consume histogram, which is milliseconds), hence unit 's'. The 'le' bucket label must stay in the by (...) clause or histogram_quantile has nothing to interpolate over. Subject to the same /health/ route-drop caveat as the request-rate panel: near-empty until traffic is driven.

panels.title: WebApi status-code mix
panels.description: Request rate broken down by HTTP response status code. Reads alongside the 5xx ratio stat: this panel shows WHICH codes are being returned, the stat shows what fraction of them are server errors. Subject to the same /health/ route-drop caveat.

panels.title: WebApi 5xx ratio
panels.description: GUARDED ON PURPOSE, AND THIS GUARD IS NOT A COPY-PASTE FROM THE FAULT STATS. On a healthy stack the 5xx numerator has no series at ALL, so an unguarded ratio returns zero samples; plan 87-05's classifier files an expression Class A in the ABSENCE of the 'or vector(0)' substring, so removing this guard would make the panel be asserted as Class A and fail the live proof (threat T-87-21). This is the ONE expression in the phase that is VER-01 Class B without being one of lint rule C3's four domain counters, which is precisely why it has its own dedicated rule - C8 - rather than an exception inside C3 or C7. Between C3, C7 and C8 no expression in this file sits in a third, lint-unenforced category. NOTE: the in-selector http_response_status_code=~"5.." is a LABEL filter, not a metric name; it is the lint's -SelfTest fixture (d), the collision case the rejected strip-clauses approach would have missed. Threshold: green base, red at 0.0001 - the value is a percentunit ratio, so 'red above 0' is a small positive epsilon (0.01% of requests), not 1.

panels.title: WebApi in-flight requests and Kestrel connections
panels.description: Concurrency and connection pressure at the WebApi edge, per pod: in-flight ASP.NET Core requests overlaid with Kestrel's active and queued connection gauges. A rising queued-connection line with flat active connections is the saturation signal. These three are gauges, so they are read directly rather than through rate(). Unlike the request-duration family these are NOT affected by the /health/ route filter (the collector drops datapoints by http.route, and none of these three carries that attribute), so this panel stays populated on an idle stack.
